claims.claim: A detector vendor's rebuttal disputes the Stanford sample (91 forum essays, 8th-grade comparison, old detector version) but still reports a 5.04% false-positive rate on 1,500+ IELTS essays — roughly one wrongful accusation in twenty (vendor with a stake).
claims.page: Are AI Checkers Biased Against Non-Native English Speakers?

claims.claim: OpenAI withdrew its own AI-text classifier within six months for low accuracy after stating at launch that reliable detection of all AI-written text is impossible.
claims.quote: It is impossible to reliably detect all AI-written text
claims.page: OpenAI's AI Text Classifier no longer available

claims.feature: machine detectors (false positives on canonical prose)
claims.claim: GPTZero flagged a section of the US Constitution and selections from the Bible as AI-generated because heavily trained-on human texts are exactly what models reproduce.
claims.quote: Selections from The Bible also show up as AI-generated
claims.page: AI Detector Believes the U.S. Constitution Was Written by AI

claims.claim: Vanderbilt disabled Turnitin's detector: even the vendor's claimed 1% false-positive rate implies about 750 wrongly flagged papers per 75,000, with extra risk to non-native writers, and reliable detection may not be possible at all.
claims.page: Guidance on AI Detection and Why We're Disabling Turnitin's AI Detector

claims.claim: Recursive paraphrasing breaks watermark, neural, zero-shot and retrieval detectors, and the best achievable detector degrades toward random as LLM text distributions approach human ones; spoofing can also make human text read as AI.
claims.source: arXiv 2303.11156 — Sadasivan et al., Can AI-Generated Text be Reliably Detected?
claims.quote: our recursive paraphrasing method can significantly reduce detection rates
claims.page: Can AI-Generated Text be Reliably Detected?

claims.claim: Unmodified GPT-4 answers submitted to five real university psychology modules went 94% undetected by markers and scored about half a grade boundary above real students.
claims.quote: 94% of our AI submissions were undetected
claims.page: A real-world test of artificial intelligence infiltration of a university examinations system

claims.claim: Across six experiments (N = 4,600) people could not detect AI self-presentations and leaned on wrong cues — first-person pronouns, contractions, family topics — which AI can exploit to read as more human than humans.
claims.page: Human heuristics for AI-generated language are flawed

claims.claim: Untrained evaluators distinguished GPT-3 stories, news and recipes from human text at chance; training lifted accuracy only to 55%, and evaluators gave contradictory reasons for their calls.
claims.quote: often contradictory reasons evaluators gave for their judgments

claims.claim: 254 Czech readers scored 55.4% without feedback, wrongly expecting AI text to be rigid and administrative and readable text to be human, and made the most errors when most confident (below chance at peak confidence).
claims.quote: make the most errors precisely when they feel most confident
claims.page: Humans can learn to detect AI-generated texts, or at least learn when they can't

claims.claim: Five heavy ChatGPT users' majority vote misclassified only 1 of 300 articles even under paraphrase and humanization, but they relied on AI vocabulary plus holistic judgments of formality, originality and clarity — not punctuation counts.
claims.page: People who frequently use ChatGPT for writing tasks are accurate and robust detectors of AI-generated text

claims.claim: 696 non-expert readers judged AI imitations of ten canonical poets more human and slightly better than the originals, because the imitations strip the ambiguity and complexity that inexperienced readers read as 'not making sense'.
claims.source: The Conversation — Jon Stone, 2024-11-15 (on Porter & Machery, Sci. Reports 2024)
claims.quote: slightly preferring the imitation to the real thing
claims.page: People can't tell the difference between human and AI-generated poetry

claims.claim: The poetry-indistinguishability result collapses under expert reading: the AI poems separate at 87.8% on formal metrics alone, paid-per-task raters were scoring comprehensibility, and imitation of known styles cannot test the innovation human poets are judged on.
claims.quote: human poets are expected to innovate on style
claims.page: A Response to 'AI-generated poetry is indistinguishable...'

claims.claim: AI-idea assistance made weaker writers' stories up to 26.6% better written and 22.6% more enjoyable, yet made stories 10.7% more similar to each other — the real failure is collective sameness, invisible in any single text's surface features.
claims.source: ScienceDaily on Doshi & Hauser, Science Advances, 2024-07-12
claims.page: AI found to boost individual creativity -- at the expense of less varied content

claims.claim: Ten professional writers applying a 14-test Torrance creative-writing rubric found LLM stories pass 3–10x fewer tests than professionals', with the deficit in originality and elaboration rather than fluency or structure; LLM judges did not correlate with the experts.
claims.page: Art or Artifice? Large Language Models and the False Promise of Creativity
